mishnayot.he: שָׁלֹשׁ אֲרָצוֹת לַשְּׁבִיעִית. כָּל שֶׁהֶחֱזִיקוּ עוֹלֵי בָבֶל, מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַד כְּזִיב, לֹא נֶאֱכָל וְלֹא נֶעֱבָד. וְכָל שֶׁהֶחֱזִיקוּ עוֹלֵי מִצְרַיִם, מִכְּזִיב וְעַד הַנָּהָר וְעַד אֲמָנָה, נֶאֱכָל, אֲבָל לֹא נֶעֱבָד. מִן הַנָּהָר וּמֵאֲמָנָה וְלִפְנִים, נֶאֱכָל וְנֶעֱבָד:
mishnayot.en: [The land of Israel is divided into] three territories with regard to the sabbatical law.[Any produce grown in land] that was occupied by those who came up from Babylon, namely from Eretz Israel as far as Chezib, may not be eaten, nor [may its soil] be cultivated. [Any produce grown in land] that was occupied by those who came up from Egypt, namely from Chezib to the river, and until Amonah, may be eaten, but [its soil] may not be cultivated. From the river till Amonah and inwards, [produce] may be eaten and [the soil] cultivated.

mishnayot.he: עוֹשִׂין בְּתָלוּשׁ בְּסוּרְיָא, אֲבָל לֹא בִמְחֻבָּר. דָּשִׁים וְזוֹרִין וְדוֹרְכִין וּמְעַמְּרִין, אֲבָל לֹא קוֹצְרִין וְלֹא בוֹצְרִין וְלֹא מוֹסְקִים. כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כָּל שֶׁכַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ מֻתָּר בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ בְּסוּרְיָא:
mishnayot.en: In Syria, one may perform work on produce that has been detached, but not on produced attached [to the soil]. They may thresh, winnow, and tread [the grapes], or make [the grain] into sheaves, but they may not harvest [the crops], nor cut the grapes, nor harvest the olives. Rabbi Akiva said this principle: the kind of work that is permitted in Eretz Israel may also be done in Syria.

mishnayot.he: בְּצָלִים שֶׁיָּרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גְּשָׁמִים וְצִמֵּחוּ, אִם הָיוּ הֶעָלִין שֶׁלָּהֶם שְׁחוֹרִין, אֲסוּרִין. הוֹרִיקוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מֻתָּרִין. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר, אִם יְכוֹלִין לְהִתָּלֵשׁ בֶּעָלִין שֶׁלָּהֶן, אֲסוּרִין. וּכְנֶגֶד כֵּן, מוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית, מֻתָּרִין:
mishnayot.en: Onions on which rain fell and which had sprouted, if their leaves had turned black, they are forbidden; if they had become green they are permitted. Rabbi Hanina ben Antigonus says: if they can be plucked out by their leaves, they are forbidden. In the year after the sabbatical year, the like of these are permitted.

mishnayot.he: מֵאֵימָתַי מֻתָּר אָדָם לִקַּח יָרָק בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה כַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ. עָשָׂה הַבַּכִּיר, הֻתַּר הָאָפִיל. רַבִּי הִתִּיר לִקַּח יָרָק בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית מִיָּד:
mishnayot.en: When may one buy vegetables at the outgoing of the sabbatical year [without fear that they are sabbatical produce]?When enough time has passed for similar [vegetables] to grow. Where produce ripens quickly, even that which is late in ripening is also permissible. Rabbi used to allow the buying of vegetables immediately after the sabbatical year was over.

mishnayot.he: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין שֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה וּפֵרוֹת שְׁבִיעִית מֵהָאָרֶץ לְחוּץ לָאָרֶץ. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, שָׁמַעְתִּי בְפֵרוּשׁ, שֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין לְסוּרְיָא וְאֵין מוֹצִיאִין לְחוּץ לָאָרֶץ:
mishnayot.en: One may not take oil [of terumah] that had to be burned, nor produce of the seventh year, from the land [of Israel] to other countries. Rabbi Shimon said: I have heard it expressly stated that they may be exported to Syria, but not to any other country outside the land.

mishnayot.he: אֵין מְבִיאִין תְּרוּמָה מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּפֵרוּשׁ, שֶׁמְּבִיאִין מִסּוּרְיָא וְאֵין מְבִיאִין מִחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ:
mishnayot.en: They may not import terumah from outside the land of Israel into Israel. Rabbi Shimon said: I have heard it expressly stated that they may be bring from Syria, but not from any other country outside the land.

english.summary: Mishnah 1 divides the land into three territories for the seventh year: what the returnees from Babylon took is neither eaten nor worked, what the returnees from Egypt took is eaten but not worked, and the inner land is both eaten and worked. Mishnah 2 says that in Syria one may work with detached produce but not attached produce, and Rabbi Akiva gives the rule that whatever is permitted in Eretz Yisrael may be done in Syria. Mishnah 3 treats onions on which rain fell and which sprouted: black leaves forbid, green ones permit, and Rabbi Hanina ben Antigonus tests whether they can be pulled out by their leaves. Mishnah 4 asks when vegetables may be bought after the seventh year, namely once similar ones have grown, and Rabbi allowed it immediately. Mishnayot 5–6 forbid taking out of the land oil of terumah that must be burned and seventh-year produce, and bringing terumah into the land from outside, with Rabbi Shimon allowing Syria.

topics.explanation: The mishnah divides the land by who took it. Territory taken by those who came up from Egypt under Joshua was holy, but its holiness ended when the Temple was destroyed. Territory retaken by those who came up from Babylon with Ezra kept its holiness. So the three territories differ in what the seventh year forbids.

Syria is the land of Aram that David conquered before he had conquered all of Eretz Yisrael. For some laws it is treated like the land and for others like outside it, so the mishnah gives it its own rules.

source.name: Bartenura
source.quote: אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם וַאֲרַם צוֹבָה שֶׁכָּבַשׁ דָּוִד, וְאֵינָהּ כְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

topics.explanation: In Syria, work on produce already cut from the ground is allowed, but cutting, harvesting grapes or olives, which is work on attached produce, is not. The reason given is to stop people from settling in Syria and leaving Eretz Yisrael.
anchors: אבל לא קוצרין ולא בוצרין ולא מוסקים

source.name: Bartenura
source.quote: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מַנִּיחִים אֶת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

topics.term: Growth of the seventh year (gidulei sheviit)
topics.explanation: Onions of the sixth year that grew in the seventh year are tested by their leaves. If the leaves turned black, new growth from the soil of the seventh year has been added and it forbids the onion. If they turned green, the onion fed itself and is permitted.

source.name: Bartenura
source.quote: אִם הִשְׁחִירוּ הֶעָלִין בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁגָּדְלוּ וְהוֹסִיפוּ, וַאֲתוּ גִּדּוּלֵי

topics.explanation: Bachir is a place that brings its produce early, and afil is the later-ripening place. After the seventh year, once the early place has produced like the old crop, the later place is permitted too, since its vegetables are presumed to come from the early place.
Oil of impure terumah that may only be burned. The mishnah forbids taking it out of the land, as with seventh-year produce, which must be removed (biur) in the land.
Seventh-year produce must be removed from the home, in the land, once the time of removal comes. That is why the mishnah does not let it leave the land.

questions.title: Where do Acco, Kziv and Amanah lie?

pasuk.text: מכזיב ועד הנהר ועד אמנה, נאכל,
pasuk.label: Mishnah Sheviit 6:1

questions.question: Bartenura describes Kziv and the 'river' as two strips extending from Acco inside the northeast corner of Eretz Yisrael. Tosafot Yom Tov asks: the mishnah never mentions Acco, so why describe the territories from it, and does the strip run from Acco or from Kziv? Rashash adds that Bartenura's reading makes even the first clause (up to Kziv) hard.

asked_by.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Sheviit 6:1:1
asked_by.quote: וקשה עכו מאן דכר שמה ולפי פירושו הוה לי' למיתני מעכו עד

asked_by.name: Rashash
asked_by.ref: Rashash on Mishnah Sheviit 6:1:1
asked_by.quote: ולכאורה יותר קשה לפירושו רישא דמתניתין דקתני כל שהחזיקו

answers.text: Tosafot Yom Tov: all three places lie on the western coast, per Kaftor VaFerach, who says he saw it himself.

sources.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
sources.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Sheviit 6:1:1
sources.quote: וכתב דעכו וכזיב ואמנה שלשתן על הים המערבי של

answers.text: Rashash: on Bartenura's view the first clause must also mean 'up to Kziv' along the same strip from Acco, and the reason they forbade it may be that it is short and was not known to all.

sources.name: Rashash
sources.quote: וטעם שגזרו עליה אולי מפני שקצרה היא שלא

questions.why: It decides where the middle territory, eaten but not worked, actually lies.
anchors: מכזיב ועד הנהר ועד אמנה, נאכל,

questions.title: What does 'eaten but not cultivated' mean?
questions.question: Bartenura brings two readings of 'not eaten and not cultivated', and Rambam gives a third. Rabbi Akiva Eiger is unsure on Bartenura's second reading whether produce may also be eaten before the removal (biur) as ordinary food, or only with the sanctity of the seventh year. How is the middle territory to be understood?

asked_by.name: Tosafot Rabbi Akiva Eiger
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Rabbi Akiva Eiger on Mishnah Sheviit 6:1:1
asked_by.quote: מסתפק במ"ל אם גם קודם הביעור מותר לאכול בתורת

answers.text: Rambam: 'not cultivated' means working the land is forbidden, and if it was worked, what grows is eaten with the sanctity of the seventh year.

sources.name: Rambam
sources.quote: ושאמר נאכל אבל לא נעבד…ואם נעבדה יהיה כל הצומח בה נאכל בקדושת

answers.text: Bartenura's main reading: 'not eaten' means not eaten after the seventh year without removal (biur), and 'not cultivated' means not worked during the seventh year.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: פֵּרוּשׁ אַחֵר וְעִקָּר, לֹא נֶאֱכָל לְאַחַר שְׁבִיעִית בְּלֹא בִעוּר, וְלֹא

answers.text: Ikar Tosafot Yom Tov, citing Rash: the restriction applies only to attached produce; detached produce may be worked, as in Syria, or else the mishnah would list four territories.

sources.name: Ikar Tosafot Yom Tov
sources.ref: Ikar Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Sheviit 6:1:2
sources.quote: וְדַוְקָא בִּמְחֻבָּר, אֲבָל בְּתָלוּשׁ עוֹשִׂין כְּמוֹ בְּסוּרְיָא דִּבְסָמוּךְ, דְּאִי לֹא

questions.why: It sets what the middle territory forbids and which kind of work.

questions.title: Why is the list of work in Syria out of order?
questions.question: The mishnah lists threshing, winnowing, treading and sheaving. Sheaving comes before threshing in the real order of work, and treading grapes is placed among the grain work. Why this order?

asked_by.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Sheviit 6:2:2
asked_by.quote: שלא כסדר מלאכתן הם שנוים…ולא ידענא טעמא מאי:

asked_by.name: Ikar Tosafot Yom Tov
asked_by.ref: Ikar Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Sheviit 6:2:1
asked_by.quote: שֶׁלֹּא כְסֵדֶר מְלַאכְתָּן הֵם שְׁנוּיִים, דְּעִמּוּר

answers.text: Hon Ashir: threshing and winnowing are normally done near the threshing floor each year, so they would look suspect, which is why they are listed with the harvest-like sheaving at the end.

sources.name: Hon Ashir
sources.quote: דהרואה יכול לדון אותו לכף זכות לומר דחיטים של

sources.name: Hon Ashir
sources.quote: דישה וזירה שדרך לעשותם סמוך לגורן מידי שנה

answers.text: Lechem Shamayim: it is also ordered by weight, each earlier item lighter than the next, in the style 'not only this but even that'.

sources.name: Lechem Shamayim
sources.quote: שכל השנויה תחלה. קלה מאותה של אחריה. דוק ותשכח.

sources.name: Lechem Shamayim
sources.quote: לא זו אף זו

answers.text: Melekhet Shelomoh quoting Rabbi Yosef: 'not only this but even that', with threshing, treading and even sheaving permitted though it looks like it comes from this field.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: לא זו אלא אף זו

questions.why: Even the order of a mishnah carries a halakhic reason, here the suspicion of onlookers.

questions.title: Does 'work on detached produce' cover people suspected on the seventh year?
questions.question: Bartenura explains that detached work is allowed in Syria even with those suspected of not keeping the seventh year, though in Eretz Yisrael one may not sort or grind with them. Melekhet Shelomoh, citing Rabbi Yosef, rejects this: would the Sages permit helping transgressors?

asked_by.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
asked_by.ref: Melekhet Shelomoh on Mishnah Sheviit 6:2:1
asked_by.quote: אין נראה לומר שיתירו חכמים לסייע לעוברי עבירה

answers.text: Bartenura (and Rash): even near the suspects, since in Eretz Yisrael one may not sort or grind with them.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ אֵצֶל הַחֲשׁוּדִים,

sources.name: Rash MiShantz
sources.quote: אפילו אצל החשודין אע"ג דבארץ תנן לא

answers.text: Rabbi Yosef in Melekhet Shelomoh: it means with non-Jews in Syria.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: אצל העובדי כוכבים אבל לא

questions.why: It sets whom one may work with and how seventh-year suspects are treated.

questions.title: Why do the onions' black leaves forbid, and what does the end of the mishnah teach?
questions.question: Rash asks about the clause 'after the seventh year the like of these are permitted': it cannot refer to onions of the seventh year itself, since those are not permitted after it. What is the clause about?

asked_by.name: Rash MiShantz
asked_by.ref: Rash MiShantz on Mishnah Sheviit 6:3:3
asked_by.quote: לא יתכן לפרש בבצלים של שביעית דהנהו

answers.text: Bartenura (and Rash): it is about onions of the sixth year that were pulled up and replanted, whose small seventh-year growth is cancelled by growth in the eighth year.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: אֶלָּא סֵיפָא נַמִּי מַיְרֵי בִּבְצָלִים שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁית שֶׁעֲקָרָן

sources.name: Rash MiShantz
sources.quote: אלא סיפא נמי בבצלין של ששית איירי

answers.text: Rashi and Rosh, per Melekhet Shelomoh: onions of the seventh year that sprouted in the eighth year are permitted if their leaves are strong.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: שאם היו של שביעית וצמחו בשמינית ויש להם כח בעלין

questions.why: It shows how growth that permits can cancel growth that forbids.

questions.title: Is the whole onion forbidden, or only the leaves?
questions.question: Bartenura says that when the leaves turn black, the growth of the seventh year cancels the original onion even though it is larger. Rabbi Akiva Eiger notes that Rambam's wording implies only the new growth is forbidden.

asked_by.name: Tosafot Rabbi Akiva Eiger
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Rabbi Akiva Eiger on Mishnah Sheviit 6:3:1
asked_by.quote: אבל הרמב"ם כתב מה שצמח מהן יהיה כאילו

answers.text: Bartenura: the seventh-year growth cancels the original onion, even though it is larger.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: וַאֲתוּ גִּדּוּלֵי שְׁבִיעִית וּמְבַטְּלִים הָעִקָּר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא

answers.text: Rambam: what grew from them is treated as grown in the land, and counts as seventh-year produce. In his Yad, only the leaves are forbidden as sefichim and the onions remain permitted.

sources.name: Rambam
sources.quote: יהיה כאילו צמח בארץ ויחשבו כפירות שביעית וזה ענין

sources.name: Tosafot Rabbi Akiva Eiger
sources.ref: Tosafot Rabbi Akiva Eiger on Mishnah Sheviit 6:3:1
sources.quote: ואותן העלים אסורים משום ספיחים. והבצלים עצמם

questions.why: It decides whether the forbidden growth takes the whole onion with it.

questions.title: Why must similar vegetables grow first, if vegetables follow the picking?
questions.question: Lechem Shamayim asks on the explanation that vegetables follow the picking: if they were picked after the seventh year they would be permitted anyway, so why wait for similar vegetables to grow?

asked_by.name: Lechem Shamayim
asked_by.ref: Lechem Shamayim on Mishnah Sheviit 6:4:1-2
asked_by.quote: א"כ למאי צריך שיעשה כיוצא בו כי היכי

answers.text: Bartenura: the permitted growth became more than the forbidden and cancelled it.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָבָה הַהֶתֵּר עַל הָאִסּוּר וְנִתְבַּטֵּל:

answers.text: Rash: although with vegetables one follows the picking, we still suspect it came from what was picked in the seventh year.

sources.name: Rash MiShantz
sources.quote: חיישינן שלא יהא מן הנלקט בשביעית

questions.why: It sets the point at which vegetables become permitted to buy.

questions.title: Why not import terumah, when bikkurim are accepted from Syria?
questions.question: Rash reports the Yerushalmi's question: Ariston brought his bikkurim from Apamea and they were accepted, so why not terumah? Why is bringing terumah forbidden?

asked_by.name: Rash MiShantz
asked_by.ref: Rash MiShantz on Mishnah Sheviit 6:6:1
asked_by.quote: הביא בכורים מאספמיא וקבלו ממנו ויביא תרומתו אמר

answers.text: Bartenura: the priests go after terumah at the threshing floors, and the Sages feared they might run outside the land to fetch it.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: חַיְשֵׁי רַבָּנָן שֶׁמָּא יִהְיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים מְרַדְּפִים אַחֲרֶיהָ וְיֵצְאוּ

answers.text: Melekhet Shelomoh: bringing terumah is not the owners' duty, but bikkurim must be brought to Jerusalem by the owners.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: שאין על הבעלים להביאה אלא מחלקים

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh

hebrew.summary: משנה א מחלקת את הארץ לשלוש ארצות לשביעית: מה שהחזיקו עולי בבל לא נאכל ולא נעבד, מה שהחזיקו עולי מצרים נאכל אך לא נעבד, ופנימה מן הנהר ומאמנה נאכל ונעבד. משנה ב: בסוריא עושים בתלוש ולא במחובר, ורבי עקיבא אומר כלל – כל שכיוצא בו מותר בארץ ישראל עושים אותו בסוריא. משנה ג: בצלים שירדו עליהם גשמים וצמחו – עלים שחורים אוסרים, הוריקו מותרים, ורבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס בודק אם יכולים להתלש בעליהם. משנה ד: מתי מותר לקחת ירק במוצאי שביעית – משיעשה כיוצא בו, ורבי התיר מיד. משניות ה-ו: אין מוציאים שמן שריפה ופירות שביעית מן הארץ לחוץ לארץ, ואין מביאים תרומה מחוץ לארץ, ורבי שמעון מתיר לסוריא.

topics.explanation: המשנה מחלקת את הארץ לפי מי שכבש אותה: עולי מצרים כבשו בימי יהושע וקדושתם בטלה, ועולי בבל עם עזרא החזיקו את הארץ וקדושתה נשארה. לכן שלוש הארצות שונות במה שהשביעית אוסרת בהן.
סוריא היא ארץ ארם שכבש דוד לפני שכבש את כל ארץ ישראל. בחלק מהדינים היא נחשבת כארץ ישראל ובחלק אחר כחוץ לארץ, ולכן המשנה קובעת לה דינים משלה.
